items.title: Keep a backup of your current data
items.do: Open Settings and choose “Export complete backup”. Keep the file somewhere safe. Do this once now and again before you try anything that restores or replaces data.
items.pass: A .guitar-academy file is saved and its size is not zero.
items.source: Completion brief §7.2: George has real data on the live site and his phone.

items.title: Play the Unit 1 question and answer
items.do: Open Continue and start the one-note lesson. Play the two bars with the reference at 60 BPM, then try one repair (start, stop a ringing note, or hold the pulse through silence) and return to both bars.
items.pass: The note (open high E), counts, muting action and hand instruction match what you actually do on the guitar, and the repair you chose made the next attempt easier.
items.source: Phase 3 gate (log, 26 Sep); Phase 5 gate review item 2.

items.title: Try the sustained-note pitch check with real input
items.do: In Strengthen, open the microphone check. Play open high E cleanly; then the B string by mistake; then a very quiet note; then a loud, overloaded one; then stay silent. Do it once in a quiet room and once with ordinary background noise.
items.pass: The clean E is identified, the wrong string is reported as a different pitch, and the quiet, overloaded and silent tries come back uncertain rather than as a match.

items.title: Try the two-pluck and E–G–E checks
items.do: In the same card, play two E plucks with a real silence between them, then without one. Then play E–G–E on the high string (frets 0–3–0), then once with the wrong middle fret (0–2–0), then with an extra pluck.
items.pass: The displayed order matches what you played; the missing silence, wrong fret and extra pluck all come back uncertain or different, never as a match.

items.title: One real review-to-retry journey
items.do: Record a temporary take in the Unit 1 lesson, compare it with the reference, and write what you intended, what you noticed and one change. Reopen it from Strengthen, do the suggested smaller exercise and return to both bars.
items.pass: The suggested exercise addresses the thing you noticed, and your next take is better in that one detail by your own judgement.

items.title: Keyboard-only pass
items.do: Without the mouse, use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Escape and the arrow keys to go through Learn, a lesson, Play, Create, Explore and Settings. On a fretboard, move with the arrow keys.
items.pass: You can reach and operate everything, you can always see where focus is, dialogs keep focus inside and Escape closes them, and focus returns to where you were.
items.source: Phase 2A-4 accessibility review: manual keyboard pass not yet performed.

items.title: VoiceOver pass
items.do: Turn on VoiceOver (Cmd+F5) and go through Continue, one lesson step, the fretboard and Settings.
items.pass: Each control is announced with a sensible name, the fretboard announces string, fret, note and relationship, and nothing important is silent.
items.source: Phase 2A-4 accessibility review: screen-reader pass not yet performed.

items.title: Installed app shows Interval and opens
items.do: Open the installed app on the Pixel (or install it from Chrome's menu). Accept an update if one is offered.
items.pass: The home-screen name and icon are Interval's, and the app opens to your existing progress.
items.source: Rename and 1 October consolidation: installed app not yet checked.

items.title: Sign in and sync after the Firebase update
items.do: In Settings, sign in with Google on the Pixel. Make a small change on the laptop (for example, favourite an activity), then reopen the app on the Pixel.
items.pass: Sign-in works, the sync status reaches synced, and the change appears on the other device.
items.source: 1 October consolidation: sign-in and sync with the refreshed SDK not verified.

items.title: Playback sounds right and stops when backgrounded
items.do: Play the Unit 1 reference on the phone speaker and on headphones. While it plays, switch to another app, then come back.
items.pass: The count-in and notes sound steady and audible, playback stops when the app goes to the background, and nothing keeps playing or overlaps when you return.

items.title: A selected lesson works offline
items.do: With a unit marked ready offline, turn on aeroplane mode, close the app fully and reopen it. Open that lesson and play it.
items.pass: The app opens, the lesson plays, and anything you save is kept and appears after you reconnect.

items.title: Refusing the microphone leaves the lesson usable
items.do: In the Unit 1 lesson, start a take and deny microphone access when Chrome asks.
items.pass: You see a clear message and can carry on with the lesson without the recording.

items.title: An update waits while you are working
items.do: After a new release, open the app while you are partway through writing a review or a sketch edit.
items.pass: The app offers the update rather than reloading by itself, and nothing you were typing is lost.

items.title: A deleted sketch stays deleted on the other device
items.do: Signed in on both devices, make a throwaway sketch, wait until it appears on the Pixel, then delete it on the laptop. Reopen the app on the Pixel.
items.pass: The sketch is gone on both devices and does not come back after either device reloads.
items.source: Plan §12 boundary table: two devices editing and deleting.

items.title: Come back on a later day without help
items.do: On a different day from your first Unit 1 success, open Continue and do the later check it offers, and answer the changed concept example in Strengthen.
items.pass: You can do the phrase and answer the changed example without looking at the earlier answer.

items.title: Notice what you came back to
items.do: After a week of normal use, look at which lessons or pieces you returned to by choice and which you avoided. Leave a feedback note on one of each.
items.pass: Two feedback notes exist: one on something you enjoyed returning to, one on something you avoided, each saying why.
items.source: Plan §10 personal trial, made non-blocking by the 20 October decisions.
